verdict.rationale: GitLab's own docs describe several self-hosting paths: a Linux package that installs GitLab without laborious configuration, official Docker images, Helm chart and Operator for cloud-native installs, self-compiling from source, and reference architectures for scaling. GitLab Self-Managed is a named deployment with instance-level controls such as turning Agent Platform on or off. Community users independently confirm running private instances, VM appliances, and the open-source core that lets anyone run or fork their own instance. Older community reports of self-managed backup bugs cover a specific version issue and do not contradict that self-hosting works. Missing for 10: explicit evidence on which AI/agent features (e.g. Duo models) run fully on self-hosted infrastructure beyond the instance-level on/off toggle.
